claims.nodeLabel: Acknowledged, unacknowledged and waived - the three states of a DoD SAP
claims.sourceText: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) category definitions applied to the alleged activity
claims.text: A legacy material-recovery and exploitation effort would map onto the taxonomy as a waived unacknowledged operations and support SAP (recovery and custody of property) with a subordinate acquisition SAP compartment (exploitation and engineering), under a single umbrella. Reasoning: the DoD definitions of operations and support SAP - expressly covering 'property' - and acquisition SAP together describe recovery-plus-reverse-engineering with no strain.

claims.nodeLabel: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)
claims.sourceText: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Glossary; DoDM 5205.07-V1 Enclosure 2 para 2.c; 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3)
claims.text: The carve-out is approvable only by the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense - no delegation to a service secretary, component head or SAPCO director is provided for in DoDD 5205.07 (2010), DoDI 5205.11 or DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1.

claims.nodeLabel: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)
claims.text: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.c: DoD SAPCO 'under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense, is established and is the primary DoD liaison with agencies of the Executive Branch and the Congress on all issues relating to DoD SAPs ... The Director, DoD SAPCO, shall be a flag officer or Senior Executive Service equivalent appointed by the Deputy Secretary of Defense.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)
claims.text: DoD SAPCO is simultaneously the office that (a) writes the criteria for reviewing waived programs, (b) confirms which contractor facilities are carved out of DCSA oversight, (c) is the single point of congressional liaison, and (d) must approve any contractor's provision of SAP material to a member of Congress. Those four functions in one office, reporting to the official who signs the waivers, is the structural definition of a closed loop. Reasoning: enumeration of the four responsibilities from DoDI 5205.11 and DoDD 5205.07.

claims.nodeLabel: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
claims.text: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.e: 'All personnel accessed to DoD SAPs shall notify the Director, DoD SAPCO, in a timely fashion, when briefing or providing DoD SAP material to any members of Congress or congressional staff. No DoD contractor entity, contractor employee, contractor representative, or consultant shall provide SAP material to any members of Congress or congressional staff without Director, DoD SAPCO, approval.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
claims.text: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.f: 'Members of Congress assigned to designated defense and intelligence committees shall be authorized access to DoD SAPs within the respective committee's SAP oversight role, except for waived programs pursuant to Reference (c). Unless approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense, only the chair, the ranking minority member, and the staff directors of the defense and intelligence committees shall be authorized access to waived SAPs within their committee's respective SAP oversight role.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
claims.text: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Glossary: 'acknowledged SAP. A SAP whose existence is acknowledged but its specific details (technologies, materials, techniques, etc.) are classified as specified in the applicable security classification guide.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
claims.text: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Enclosure 2 para 5: 'When the Secretary of Defense determines that national security would be adversely affected if SAP data is reported to Congress using standard processes, he or she may designate select unacknowledged SAPs as waived in accordance with Reference (c).'

claims.nodeLabel: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
claims.text: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.h: 'All waived SAP material submitted to Congress, to include annual reports and other products, shall remain in DoD custody. No copies shall be stored outside DoD repositories or control without the approval of the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
claims.text: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Glossary: 'carve-out. A provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense that relieves DSS of its National Industrial Security Program obligation to perform industrial security oversight functions for a DoD SAP.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
claims.text: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Glossary: 'unacknowledged SAP. A SAP having protective controls ensuring the existence of the program is not acknowledged, affirmed, or made known to any person not authorized for such information.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
claims.text: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Glossary: 'waived SAP. A SAP for which the Secretary of Defense has waived applicable reporting in accordance with Reference (c) following a determination of adverse effect to national security. An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls.'

claims.nodeLabel: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
claims.text: Paragraph 4.e is a documented gag on contractor-to-Congress disclosure: a cleared contractor employee cannot lawfully hand SAP material to a member of Congress without the approval of the Director, DoD SAPCO - the very office whose programs would be the subject of the disclosure. Reasoning: the approval authority and the subject of the disclosure are the same office.

DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.b: 'The Special Access Program Oversight Committee (SAPOC), hereby established, shall advise and assist the Secretary of Defense (SecDef) and the Deputy Secretary of Defense with governance, management, and oversight of DoD SAPs.'

claims.nodeLabel: The annual DoD special access program report to Congress
claims.text: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Enclosure 2 para 6: 'The CAs shall prepare and submit annual reports and other required SAP information through the Director, DoD SAPCO, and the governance structure in order to report the state of DoD SAPs to congressional committees, in accordance with Reference (c).'
